questions.q: What are the four golden signals from the Google SRE book?
options: Latency, traffic, errors, saturation
Metrics, logs, traces, alerts
CPU, memory, disk, network
Uptime, downtime, MTTR, MTTD
questions.explain: The four golden signals are latency, traffic, errors, and saturation — the highest-value starting point for monitoring almost any service.

questions.q: Why should you track successful and failed request latency separately rather than one blended average?
options: Because failed requests are always slower than successful ones
Because blended averages are illegal under most SLAs
Because only successful requests count as traffic
Because a fast failure (like an instant 500 error) can pull the blended average down and hide real slowness in successful requests
questions.explain: A fast-failing request lowers a blended average, making the service look healthy even though successful requests might be taking far longer than acceptable.

questions.q: A service returns HTTP 200 but with an empty response body due to a bug. Which golden signal captures this as a failure, and why does it matter?
options: Errors, but only if you track implicit failures (wrong content), not just explicit status codes
Saturation, because empty responses indicate the server is full
Traffic — because empty responses are a traffic problem
Latency, because empty responses are always fast
questions.explain: An implicit error (wrong content with a success status code) is still a failure. A status-code-only error metric would miss it entirely.

questions.q: In the Northbridge flash-sale sequence, which golden signal gave the EARLIEST warning, before latency or errors moved?
options: Saturation (connection pool filling up)
Traffic
Errors
Latency
questions.explain: Saturation — the connection pool filling toward capacity — climbed before latency and errors did, making it the earliest leading indicator.

questions.q: Why is traffic volume important context for interpreting the other three signals?
options: The same latency increase means something very different at 10x normal traffic than at normal traffic
Traffic has no relationship to the other signals
Traffic is the only signal worth monitoring
Traffic replaces the need for saturation monitoring
questions.explain: Traffic provides context: a latency bump during a known traffic spike (like a flash sale) is interpreted differently than the same bump under normal load.
